items.title: US Navy escorts oil tanker through Strait of Hormuz, Wright says

featured_image.name: US offers navy escort for oil tankers passing through Strait ...

items.description:
Energy Secretary Chris Wright announced on March 10 that the US Navy had successfully escorted an oil tanker through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first confirmed military-assisted transit since the waterway was effectively shut down by Iran's threats following the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran.[1]

Wright's announcement, posted on social media, offered few details about the operation and did not specify whether a broader escort program was now underway. The move comes after days of promises from President Trump and senior administration officials that the Navy would protect commercial shipping through the strait, which handles roughly 20% of the world's crude oil supply.[2][3][1]

items.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic hits crisis low despite Western efforts to restart shipping

featured_image.name: Only a handful of ships risk Strait of Hormuz transit — who ...

items.description: Nearly two weeks after the U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran effectively shut down one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints, commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains at a near-standstill — though a handful of vessels have begun testing the waters under extraordinary risk, and a growing coalition of Western governments is working to reopen the waterway.

items.title: Aramco says it can restore output 'in days' once Hormuz reopens

featured_image.name: Aramco sees 'catastrophic consequences' for oil if shipping doesn't resume in Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Saudi Aramco warned Tuesday of "catastrophic consequences" for global oil markets if the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, even as CEO Amin Nasser said the company could ramp production back up "in days, not weeks" once shipping resumes through the vital waterway.[1][2]

Speaking on the company's fourth-quarter earnings call, Nasser said Aramco expects to reach the full 7-million-barrel-per-day capacity of its East-West pipeline within days, rerouting crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu to partially bypass the strait. The company also said its Ras Tanura complex — home to Saudi Arabia's largest refinery and a major offshore oil-loading terminal — was restarting after a precautionary shutdown following an Iranian drone attack last week.[1]

items.title: IEA calls for emergency oil reserve release at G7 meeting

featured_image.name: G7 holds off on tapping oil reserves amid Middle East war

items.description: The International Energy Agency called for a coordinated release of emergency oil reserves during a meeting with G7 finance ministers on Monday, marking a dramatic reversal from its position just days earlier that no such action was needed, as the war in Iran continues to choke off global energy supplies through the Persian Gulf.

items.title: Musk says X Money will enter early public access in April

featured_image.name: X taps William Shatner to give out invites to its payments service, X Money

items.description: Elon Musk announced on Tuesday that X Money, the digital payment system built into his social media platform X, will enter early public access next month. The confirmation, posted on X on March 10, marks the clearest timeline yet for a product central to Musk's long-stated ambition to transform the platform into an "everything app."[1][2][3]

items.title: Hegseth vows 'most intense' strikes yet as Iran war hits day 10

featured_image.name: Hegseth touts U.S. success in Iran war and takes questions on Operation  Epic Fury

items.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared Tuesday that Iran is "badly losing" as the United States prepared to unleash the heaviest bombardment yet in its 10-day-old campaign against the Islamic Republic, vowing that the day would bring "the most fighters, the most bombers, the most strikes" of Operation Epic Fury.[1][2]

Speaking at a Pentagon briefing alongside Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine, Hegseth said Iran's military capacity is deteriorating rapidly while its regional allies have abandoned it. "Iran stands alone and they are badly losing on day 10 of Operation Epic Fury," Hegseth said.[3]

items.title: Iran hits Israel, Gulf states as conflict enters 11th day

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Tehran vows to use powerful missiles, rejects Trump talks

items.description: Iran continued its barrage of drone and missile strikes against Israel and Gulf Arab nations on Monday and Tuesday, as the conflict triggered by the joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran entered its 11th day with no clear end in sight.

items.title: YouTube extends deepfake detection tool to politicians and journalists

featured_image.name: AI models spot deepfake images, but people catch fake videos

items.description:
YouTube announced Tuesday that it is opening its AI-powered likeness detection technology to a pilot group of government officials, political candidates, and journalists, giving public figures new tools to identify and report deepfake videos that use their faces without permission.[1][2]

The expansion marks the first time the platform has extended the tool beyond its creator community, where it launched last year for roughly 4 million members of the YouTube Partner Program.[3][1]

items.title: Iran war fuels global debate over shift to renewables

featured_image.name: Iran war threatens prolonged hit to global energy markets ...

items.description: As the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran enters its second week, the conflict's disruption of global energy markets is fueling a debate over whether soaring oil and gas prices could accelerate the world's transition to renewable energy. With oil having briefly surged past $100 a barrel and European natural gas prices spiking, leaders from the European Union to the United Nations are framing clean energy not just as a climate imperative but as a matter of national security.
